heard: A multi-ton NASA telescope pivots in seconds without human commands. Most missions wait days for human planning, but Swift launched in 2004 to act alone. It carries three coalined instruments to catch gamma-ray flashes that last mere seconds. The mission was named for the Swift bird, which pivots mid-flight to rapidly change direction. A mask of 52,000 lead tiles calculates the coordinates of the blast. Within 100 seconds, the spacecraft autonomously slews its entire body to focus its lens. This caught a dying star 13 billion light years away, when the universe was 630 million years old. Built for a two-year mission, the observatory spent two decades hunting these flashes.
